title: Stage publication under the release-candidate dist-tag, and move latest as a separate recorded, reversible step (Article 3.5)
description: Constitution Article 3 clause 5 (opum-ai/opum-agent 73ba142, ratified 2026-09-27; opum-agent ruling bf4fd4b4): both package families publish first under the release-candidate dist-tag, opum-cli-e2e qualifies that staged pair from clean registry installs, and latest moves only after that, Quest first. Registry publication is irreversible, so a failure rolls back dist-tags to their recorded prior values, never unpublishes. Today both publishers (scripts/publish-release.mjs and release.yml) run npm publish with no --tag, so every publish moves latest immediately.

acceptanceCriteria.text: scripts/publish-release.mjs and release.yml publish every one of the seven tarballs with --tag release-candidate, and a test fails if either publish invocation omits it

A promote step moves latest to the version on all seven packages (platforms first, wrapper last), records every prior latest value before it moves any tag, and refuses unless all seven are already published at that version under release-candidate
A rollback restores every tag the promote step moved to its recorded prior value, and is exercised by a test
The runbook describes stage, qualify, promote and rollback in that order

plan: 1. A shared STAGE_TAG and one publishArgs helper that every npm publish call in publish-release.mjs goes through, --diagnose-staged re-attempt included (it is a real write and would otherwise move latest)
2. release.yml: --tag release-candidate on both npm publish lines; a test reads the workflow and fails on any npm publish without it

3. scripts/promote-release.mjs: read the dist-tags of all seven anonymously, refuse unless release-candidate is the version on all seven, write the prior-latest record BEFORE moving any tag, move latest platforms-first then wrapper, restore on a mid-way failure, verify by re-read; --rollback <record> restores every recorded prior value
4. Tests for promote, rollback and mid-way failure with injected npm and registry reads
finalSummary:
Every quest publish now STAGES under the release-candidate dist-tag, and latest moves only through a separate, recorded, reversible step (constitution Article 3.5, opum-ai/opum-agent 73ba142).

Changed:
- scripts/publish-release.mjs: one publishArgs helper builds every npm publish argument list, with --tag release-candidate, including the --diagnose-staged re-attempt, which is a real write and would otherwise have moved latest. The success line says the release is staged and latest is unmoved.
- release.yml: --tag release-candidate on both npm publish lines.
- scripts/promote-release.mjs (new): reads the dist-tags of all seven packages anonymously, from registry.npmjs.org/-/package/<name>/dist-tags. It refuses unless release-candidate is the version on all seven, and it writes every prior latest to --record BEFORE moving any tag. It then moves latest platforms first and the wrapper last. On a mid-way failure it restores the tags that run moved. It verifies by an anonymous re-read with a bounded wait. --rollback <record> restores every recorded prior value. The record is written once, with exclusive create, and a rerun reuses it, because after a partial move the registry already reads the new version. A fresh plan refuses to record the new version as the prior one (lost-record guard).
- Runbook: a "Stage, qualify, promote" section in that order, plus rollback. CHANGELOG: an Unreleased entry.

Verified:
- test/qcli385-stage-under-release-candidate.test.ts, 14 tests: publishArgs, a source-level count proving every publish goes through publishArgs, release.yml publish lines (count asserted, so it cannot pass vacuously), plan refusal on one unstaged package, unreadable tags, the lost-record guard and resume, platforms-first promotion, mid-way failure restoring exactly the moved tags with the wrapper untouched, rollback after full promotion, record validation, and verify lag and timeout.
- Mutation control: removing --tag from one release.yml line and from publishArgs turned exactly the 2 predicted tests red; restored, 14/14.
- A live dry run against the real registry refused correctly: release-candidate is 0.2.9 on all seven, and 0.10.0 was never staged. No record was written.
- bun run check exited 0: typecheck, lint, format, layers, and 744 tests at that point.

Not in scope: the latest move is not yet gated on opum-cli-e2e's registry-install PASS. That is QCLI-388, per opum-agent ruling A on OPAG-465.
